Hromokley Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kirovohrad Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Hromokley was founded in 1857 by 16 Jewish families as an agricultural colony, growing to 334 people across 48 households by 1896, with a synagogue and cheder by the century's end. According to local tradition, the mother of Leon Trotsky, the Bolshevik revolutionary leader, was buried in this cemetery — a claim attributed to local testimony rather than independently confirmed. The community suffered through pogroms in 1918–19 and starvation and Spanish flu in 1921–22; the synagogue closed in 1927, and the vast majority of Hromokley's Jews were murdered during the Holocaust. The village itself ceased to exist after 1970. This cemetery was demolished around the 1960s-70s to make space for agriculture, according to local residents.
